sources.title: Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction in Motivating Adults to Dance Lindy Hop
sources.authors: Bretting K, Wallhead TL, Wilson M, Zhu Q.
sources.journal: Journal of dance medicine & science : official publication of the International Association for Dance Medicine & Science

sources.title: Moving with meaning: community line dancing, health-motivated engagement, and belonging among older adults in Texas

findings.finding: Lindy Hop participation helps satisfy the basic psychological needs required for sustained dance motivation.
findings.quote: satisfy the 3 basic psychological needs required for internalized motivation that contributes to sustained dance participation.

findings.finding: Older adults experience autonomy through lifelong passion, continuous learning, and self-directed engagement.
findings.quote: Participants experienced autonomy through self-directed engagement in dance, including lifelong passion, ongoing learning, and leadership within dance groups.

findings.finding: Competence is built through skill confidence and bodily self-awareness, reinforced by peer recognition.
findings.quote: Competence was reflected in skill confidence and bodily self-awareness, supported by peer recognition and opportunities to contribute to the group.

principle: Satisfying learners' basic psychological needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness fosters motivation and sustained participation.
for_the_teacher: Give learners choices in their practice to support their sense of autonomy.
Build competence by highlighting skill confidence and bodily self-awareness.
Foster a sense of relatedness and community connection during lessons.
